Episode 142. Negotiations (1)
The Tower of White Night.
The Tower of White Night, which always emitted a subtle light even in the middle of the desolate desert, had lost its power and appeared miserable due to the Sota Desert incident.
On the rooftop with a huge hole, three elderly people and a dragon transformed into a human stood.
Kelliark, Kadun, Octavia, and Hedo were sitting in chairs created by Kelliark's magic, looking out over the Sota Desert.
The desert was still full of traces of battle.
Due to the underground construction yard explosion, the middle of the desert had sunk completely, forming a grotesque and enormous crater. The blowing sandstorm was filled with sparks and heat.

Flames and lightning that had risen like tumors all over the desert had been suppressed for several days, but there was no sign of them ending. The remains of dead dragons and destroyed airships were scattered all around.
Twelve dragons had been killed, 43 airships had been destroyed, eight members of the Specter Squad and almost 250 wizards had died.
And they had some airship blueprints and 'machines' stolen.
"It's the first time since the Kingdom Defense War 500 years ago that the family has suffered this much damage."
As Kelliark spoke softly, Kadun chuckled.
"It was incomparable to this at that time."
Although he spoke as if it was nothing, Kadun was the most disturbed among them.
The re-emergence of the Archduke's family of the demon world and Murakan, who seemed to have regained much of his old power, were two factors that made Kadun feel frustrated.
In many ways, it felt like a nightmare coming back to life.
Of course, Murakan had only regained about half of his martial prowess from his heyday, but those who had heard Hedo's report were under the impression that he had regained more.
The misunderstanding of Murakan's martial prowess, which began with the Black King's Party incident, continued to grow in this way.
"Considering that Run Kandell managed to escape even though you were there, it seems that Kadun is not afraid of Murakan for no reason."
"No, when did I get scared?"
"You said that last time. It was right after the Black King's Party incident."
"Why would you say that in a place with people around?"
"…Not only the riders and Murakan, but also Kinzelo and their demons were a problem. From the circumstances, it seems that the demon called Bianca Caligo injured Sir Hedo."
At Octavia's additional explanation, Kelliark and Kadun nodded.
"Bianca Caligo, unlike Ainas Caligo, showed first-class superhuman strength. It is believed that the damage was limited to this extent because Sir Hedo was there."

"That's right, if Hedo hadn't been there, this place would have disappeared without a trace, Kelliark. And your daughter would have been killed or become an enemy's experimental subject or a prisoner."

"Her judgment to evacuate all the forces in the magic tower in advance was also excellent. If everyone had been there, it would have been a massacre. Because of that, I think my subordinates are a little resentful of Sir Hedo..."
"Your daughter occasionally makes outstanding judgments with strange intuition. It's the only thing Sandra has in common with you."
Hedo's gaze remained fixed on the distant desert without saying a word.
Although he had started lying for the first time in his life since he began serving Sandra, this was the first time for such a serious matter.
"If you have a request, please speak, Sir Hedo."
"I am grateful enough that you do not hold me responsible for failing to protect the vault."
"That was not your fault. So, please speak."
"…I would be grateful for a few days off, including the young lady."
Kelliark grinned. Hedo found it burdensome to meet the seemingly all-knowing gaze of Kelliark.
"Very well. You may take ten days off and leave immediately."
"Then I will return after the trip, Master."
As soon as Kelliark finished speaking, Hedo immediately left the place.
It was because he found it increasingly uncomfortable to continue lying. The remaining companions admired Hedo's dignified appearance.
"I like Sir Hedo's confident demeanor."
"That man is definitely a treasure of the Zipfel family, Kelliark. You must hold onto him and make sure he doesn't change his mind."
"Yes, I must. Anyway…"
Kelliark's gaze reached the area between the Lomin Forest and the central border.
At the end of the battle, Joshua spread the volcano, and even then, the recovery forces had not yet properly accessed the area.
"That power was surely the power of Chaos, wasn't it, Octavia?"
"Yes, Master."
"Runcandel and Chaos... Both the infiltration and the power he showed at the end. With this, the evidence is conclusive. The Harbinger of Calamity is with Runcandel."
The Harbinger of Calamity.
Since Solderet disappeared, Zipfel had been continuously pursuing her.
As far as Zipfel knew, the last time Solderet communicated with a human was with their former Master, Liol Zipfel.
There were records of contractors since then, but none of them mentioned communicating with Solderet.
Therefore, Zipfel had assumed that Solderet had lost her power, or had sealed herself away to avoid breaking the pact.
That was the case until Jin appeared, and until evidence emerged that the Harbinger of Calamity was with Runcandel.
"And the fact that Joshua Runcandel used the power of the Harbinger so blatantly implies that Chiron has reached the territory of the Five Black Sea Kings."

"Yes, Master. Chiron Runcandel would never have allowed the use of such an unstable power. However, it's surprising that he didn't know about the Harbinger's existence... It's now proven that he turned a blind eye to it. Did he think there was no other way?"
"No, that's not it. He isn't weak enough to rely on something other than himself, that monster."
"Then why…?"
"Well, perhaps he expected his children and relatives to overcome even the calamity's prophecy through Runcandel's value and struggle."

"Even though he knows that when his time is up and we regain our old power, Runcandel will inevitably be destroyed. Would he have made such a choice in the midst of that? I think he must have had some hope in the prophecy."
"He is different from us. He is an old-fashioned man."
Suddenly, Kelliark's appearance began to become younger.
His wrinkled face and the back of his hands smoothed out, his rough hair regained its luster. No one would have recognized that the mischievous-looking boy was Kelliark Zipfel.

"Anyway, we can't start a full-scale war based on just the suspicion that Chiron has entered the territory of the Five Black Sea Kings. Moreover, as confirmed by this incident, the enemy's strength surpasses our expectations."
Runcandel and Kinzelro.
Through this incident, Zipfel had once again confirmed their power. The power of the Prophet of Calamity, the demon dragon, and the power of the demon nobility, among others.
And even that might not be all.

"It's a bit painful to pay the price of arrogance gained from ruling as the world's number one family for a thousand years. Even though we intentionally lured them in to check their power, we are the ones who suffered the most damage."

"Heh, look at that. I've been telling you over and over again that it's not the time to leisurely stare at an invisible crystal ball. They stole the blueprints and machines, so they'll become stronger."
"That's why I'm going to be a little more careful in the future. We have to speed up all of our plans."

Completing the Magic Stone, confirming whether Chiron entered the territory of the Five Black Sea Kings, verifying and reinterpreting the exact content of the prophecies held by Runcandel, restoring the ancient civilization, grasping the true nature of Solderet, tracking down Temar's tomb, and more.
For the acceleration and realization of all these tasks, one person was absolutely needed.
"We will invest more manpower and resources in finding the last survivor of the Hister family."
"Do we have the manpower to spare for that right now? When will all that be restored?"
"It means you have to look harder, Kadun."
"Ah, I'm so frustrated!"
"I should move a bit too..."
"Really!? Are you not going to waste time looking at the crystal ball anymore?"
"Yes."
Valeria Hister.
She was the key to all the great powers. The key to victory, the key to delaying defeat, the key to gaining new opportunities.
"Maybe I'll have to sit down at the negotiating table with Rosa Runcandel again. If we meet again for Hister's case, it will inevitably be a much worse deal than before."
Kinzelro Main Office.
Most of the senior executives, including Bishkel and Berakt, were looking alternately at the tightly closed chief's office and the warship Grenil anchored behind it.

Since the incident at the Black Emperor's Castle, the chief had never properly woken up. But this time, both the Zeppelin and the warship Grenil used his power, so the chief's condition continued to worsen.
Squeak, thud! Kududududud...!
The damaged Grenil screamed as it dropped parts even when standing still, making the officers' feelings more complicated.
"So, our vice-commander used me as a perfect bait there. I've never seen such a cunning human before."
"Hahaha, Vice-commander Bishkel seems cold-blooded, but he's really a nice person. He even buys me sweet potato croquettes every time."

"Oh, this is delicious. I'll have to ask for it every day from now on. Anyway, if the vice-commander hadn't used me as bait there, I would've been captured. Those humans, they were stronger than I thought... Uh, but they're still like mayflies compared to our sister."
"Let's toast for Bishkel!"
"Alright, Bubare! A toast to sweet potato croquettes!"
Only two people, Bubare and Ainas, were excitedly chatting.
Ainas didn't know that she had never been used as bait, and Bishkel had simply found it a waste to use the ship's power to save her.
In the end, it was true that Ainas was saved.

Following the signal flare of the zeppelin, the ship Grenil and Bianca moved, and while Zipfel pursued them, Joshua caused the volcano to erupt, quickly making Ainas forgotten by everyone on the battlefield.
As the two laughed and chatted loudly, Bishkel was really losing hair.
Seeing a handful of hair caught in his palm, it was difficult for him to suppress the urge to cut their throats.
"Stop bothering the poor vice-commander, you demon bastards."
Zeppelin grabbed Bubare and Ainas' hair.

"Right, even if you like your older sister, you should know when enough is enough. And it's not just because of this incident that the commander is lying down, but also because he healed Bubare. Shouldn't we be a little quieter today?"
Margiella also stood next to Zeppelin and spoke.

"You two should probably go over there and crouch down. I'm furious at being played by Jin Runcandel, and on top of that, Joshua Runcandel, whom we tried to capture as a hostage, even blew himself up... You understand? My mood. It's really, really bad."
At Zeppelin's words, Bubare and Ainas disappeared somewhere with a quick step, sweating.
"That... I'm sorry. Your Excellency. My sister... but she's good."
"I know, I know, Princess Bianca."
"I'm sorry, sorry."
Bianca bowed her head repeatedly in apology and hurriedly disappeared after her sister.
Zeppelin let out a deep sigh and couldn't help but wonder if they were really the ones to shoulder the future of the demon race.
"What are you going to do now, Zeppelin?"
As Margiella asked, Zeppelin gritted his teeth.
"I'll have to negotiate with Jin Runcandel, that damn human. If he plays with me again this time, I'll find a way to kill him no matter what..."
